QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_31

question.text: What is 'reverse cash and carry arbitrage'?

answer.text: When futures are underpriced, sell (short) the underlying in spot, invest the proceeds at the risk-free rate, and buy (long) futures to lock in profit
The opposite of any arbitrage trade — accepting a loss to maintain a position
Buying futures and simultaneously buying the underlying for double exposure
Converting futures positions to options positions to reduce risk

explanation.text: The Logic: If futures trade below their fair or theoretical price, the arbitrageur buys the futures, sells or shorts the underlying in the cash market, and invests or lends the sale proceeds at the risk-free rate where applicable. At expiry, the cash position is unwound against the futures to lock in the mispricing as profit. The Trap: This is a defined arbitrage strategy that exploits underpriced futures; it is not a way to accept losses, not a doubled directional bet, and not a conversion of futures into options. Note: Feasibility in practice depends on the ability to borrow the underlying for short selling and on the associated stock-borrowing and transaction costs.
